title: PHILIPPE LAFFONT'S COATUE JUST UPDATED ITS STOCK PORTFOLIO
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
Coatue went shopping in software and memory. Microsoft (MSFT) was more  
than doubled (+119.93%) to $3.31B, Meta (META) was boosted 78.72% to  
$3.27B, and they opened a $1.84B stake in Salesforce (CRM), a $1.75B  
ADR line in SK Hynix (SKHY), and $1.16B of Shopify (SHOP). They also  
started new Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), Visa (V) and Mastercard  
(MA) positions. On the other side, they sold out of a $1.15B Forgent  
(FPS) stake and cut Cerebras (CBRS) by 53.56%.  
  
Here are the top holdings as of the end of Q3:  
  
\- $4.31B of TSMC (TSM) (added 5.86%)  
\- $3.49B of Micron (MU) (added 4.22%)  
\- $3.31B of Microsoft (MSFT) (added 119.93%)  
\- $3.27B of Meta (META) (added 78.72%)  
\- $3.26B of Lam Research (LRCX) (added 5.13%)  
\- $2.94B of SpaceX (SPCX) (added 4.82%)  
\- $2.89B of Amazon (AMZN) (cut 1.83%)  
\- $2.34B of Broadcom (AVGO) (added 14.02%)  
\- $2.34B of GE Vernova (GEV) (cut 3.77%)  
\- $2.31B of Applied Materials (AMAT) (added 7.18%)  
\- $1.88B of Intel (INTC) (added 29.53%)  
\- $1.84B of Salesforce (CRM) (new)  
\- $1.75B of SK Hynix (SKHY) (new)  
\- $1.61B of Eaton (ETN) (cut 24.58%)  
\- $1.51B of Equinix (EQIX) (added 17.15%)  
\- $1.48B of Alphabet (GOOGL) (cut 11.71%)  
\- $1.43B of Nvidia (NVDA) (added 3.25%)  
\- $1.18B of Constellation Energy (CEG)  
\- $1.16B of Shopify (SHOP) (new)  
\- $1.00B of Natera (NTRA)  
\- $997M of Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) (new)  
\- $926M of Visa (V) (new)  
\- $883M of Mastercard (MA) (new)  
\- $837M of Hut 8 (HUT)  
\- $639M of Spotify (SPOT)  
\- $578M of Cerebras (CBRS) (cut 53.56%)  
  
Sold out: Forgent (FPS), Caris Life Sciences, AMD (AMD)  
  
Holdings are as of September 30, per Coatue's Q3 13F filing. 13Fs only  
cover long U.S.-listed positions and lag the market, so the fund may  
have changed these since then. Coatue reported 73 equity positions  
worth $54.5B.  
  
The Microsoft, Meta, Salesforce, SK Hynix and Shopify adds look like a  
clear software-and-memory push. Which of those new or doubled-up lines  
do you find most interesting?
